item.title: LLM (Claude) Given Robotic Hand Immediately Starts Making Peace Signs
item.description: An LLM just opened and closed a robotic hand on its own, and watched it happen through a camera. There’s a 3D-printed robotic hand sitting on a desk here. An LLM (Claude) is controlling it. The AI spotted the hand through a USB camera, found the serial port, connected to the firmware, and started running […]

item.title: Attempting to detect smart glasses nearby and warn you
item.description: Yves Jeanrenaud has created an app, Nearby Glasses, which attempts to detect smart glasses nearby and warn you. It is available on Google Play. This app notifies you when smart glasses are nearby. It uses company identificators in the Bluetooth data sent out by these. Therefore, there likely are false positives (e.g. from VR headsets). […]

item.title: Watch This Backpack Automatically Deploy an Umbrella in the Rain
item.description: In Seattle if you carry an umbrella you get some dirty looks. I wonder how soggy Seattleites would respond to Current Concepts wearable self-deploying backpack umbrella? When rain is detected via a resistive rain sensor the umbrella pops open. It all runs off and ESP32 microcontroller. Fun video full of punchy quips. Write up from […]

item.title: 80386 Protected Mode deep dive
item.description: nand2mario on the Small Things Retro blog is building an 80386-compatible core in SystemVerilog and blogging the process. The 80286 introduced “Protected Mode” in 1982. It was not popular. The mode was difficult to use, lacked paging, and offered no way to return to real mode without a hardware reset. The 80386, arriving three years […]

item.description: Over on 0x19.co, they’ve ported the game Doom to yet another device, a 20-year-old Snom 360 office phone.
